purpose: Prove the complete FT-008 manual-payment lifecycle and operator surface through the real local runtime and built-in Admin browser flow.
success_outcome: A sanitized backend/browser run demonstrates correct lifecycle state, reservation/inventory behavior, required Admin fields, and safe duplicate/terminal handling.
anti_goals: Do not use live payment/provider mutation or production data.
Do not alter feature source to satisfy a report-only assertion or hide a native Admin mismatch.
Do not implement FT-009 return/webhook UI or FT-010 email behavior.

forbidden_scope: YooKassa live calls, credentials, webhook transport, return-page authority
production data, secrets, cookies, tokens, direct database browser access

success_checks: Real compiled Medusa/PostgreSQL runtime proves pending_payment through Admin-confirmed paid, processing, completed, native pending/paid cancellation, cancellation-origin refund, and standalone refund behavior.
Built-in Admin/browser order detail shows every required operator field with synthetic content.
Current checkout persists personal_request and a controlled legacy fixture preserves card/sbp/sberpay only as a historical offline-request label without a provider call.

Admin-confirmed payment preserves reservations, fulfillment consumes them, native cancellation persists the order and applies native refund/reservation-cleanup semantics, duplicate/terminal events do not mutate twice, and no provider request occurs.

The runtime/browser acceptance proves Store, customer, unauthenticated, and unauthorized-Admin lifecycle attempts are denied, cross-order and forged event references fail closed, and concurrent or out-of-order events cannot mutate a terminal order.

The built-in metadata editor and direct Admin API cannot change or delete any protected workflow key, explicitly including checkout_reservation_item_ids and checkout_reservation_line_ids, while unrelated operator metadata remains editable.

Partial refunds preserve logical state and only persisted native refunds (or authoritative raw_refunded_amount) covering all persisted native captures (or raw_captured_amount) project refunded, without assuming a capture/refund status field.
Cleanup, privacy, and recovery assertions are runtime-observed rather than report-only.
evidence_required: Browser/Admin trace or report for required fields and state projection.

Sanitized negative-path report for authorization denial, allow-listing, same-order binding, cancellation-origin/single partial/cumulative partial/final full refunds, every protected workflow key including checkout_reservation_item_ids and checkout_reservation_line_ids, late/terminal events, duplicate/replay, and concurrent transition races.
Privacy, cleanup, typecheck/build/lint, and full T3 closure evidence.

stop_conditions: The real Admin/browser boundary cannot be exercised with an existing local synthetic operator setup.
Evidence cannot prove native reservation consumption and no duplicate/terminal mutation.
Acceptance requires a new production auth/bearer mechanism or live provider credentials.
A discovered implementation defect requires edits outside the scoped lifecycle/Admin acceptance files.
